stem: What does a receipts and payments account of a club show?

options.content: A summary of the cash received and paid in the period
options.rationale: Correct: it records cash movements only.

options.content: The surplus or deficit of the club for the whole year
options.rationale: That is the income and expenditure account.

options.content: The assets and liabilities of the club at the year end
options.rationale: That is the statement of financial position.

options.content: The profit made on each of the club's separate activities
options.rationale: Separate trading accounts show activity profits.

explanation: A receipts and payments account is a summary of cash received and paid with opening and closing balances.

stem: How is the accumulated fund of a club calculated?

options.rationale: Correct: it is the net assets of the club.

options.content: Income less expenditure for the year
options.rationale: That is the surplus or deficit.

options.content: Bank and cash less the amounts owing
options.rationale: All assets are included, not just cash.

options.content: The total of the subscriptions received in the year
options.rationale: Subscriptions are only one source of income.

explanation: Accumulated fund = total assets − total liabilities, the club's equivalent of capital.

stem: Which one of the following does NOT appear in a receipts and payments account?

options.rationale: Cash received is a receipt.
Correct: depreciation is not a cash payment.
A capital payment is shown with other payments.
Opening cash and bank balances are shown.

explanation: Depreciation is not a movement of cash, so it is not in the cash summary.

stem: A club has equipment US\$7,800, bank US\$2,480, cash US\$110, subscriptions in arrears US\$260 and inventory US\$350. It owes US\$180 for expenses and has received subscriptions of US\$90 in advance. What is the accumulated fund?

options.rationale: This ignores the liabilities.
All the assets, not only cash and bank, are included.
The liabilities are added instead of deducted.
Correct: assets 11,000 less liabilities 270.

hints: Add all the assets, then deduct all the liabilities.

stem: A club buys new sports equipment for cash. How is the payment dealt with when the receipts and payments account is converted to an income and expenditure account?

options.content: It is charged in full as an expense of the year of purchase
options.rationale: Equipment lasts for several years, so it is a capital item.

options.content: It is added to the subscriptions income of the year
options.rationale: Payments are not income.

options.content: It is not an expense; depreciation is charged instead
options.rationale: Correct: it is capital expenditure.

options.content: It is ignored and no depreciation is charged later
options.rationale: Depreciation is a charge for using the asset.

explanation: Equipment is capital expenditure; only the depreciation is an expense.

stem: A club received subscriptions of US\$6,840. Arrears were US\$230 at the start and US\$370 at the end. Subscriptions received in advance were US\$135 at the start and US\$165 at the end. What is the subscriptions income for the year?

options.rationale: The receipts must be adjusted for arrears and advances.
Every adjustment has the wrong sign.
The advance at the start is added, not deducted.

hints: Arrears at the end add to income; advances at the end reduce it.

stem: A club paid US\$3,600 for hall hire in the year. US\$200 was owing at the start of the year and US\$260 is owing at the end. What is the hall hire expense in the income and expenditure account?

options.rationale: The accruals have the wrong signs.
The expense must be adjusted for the amounts owing.
Neither accrual is simply added.

explanation: Expense = cash paid − opening accrual + closing accrual = 3,660.
hints: Remove last year's amount and add this year's.

stem: A club's accumulated fund at the start of the year was US\$24,800. In the year it had a deficit of US\$3,200 and no other changes. What is the accumulated fund at the end?

options.rationale: A deficit must be deducted, not added.
Correct: a deficit reduces the fund.
This is only the deficit.
The deficit changes the fund.

stem: A receipts and payments account shows the surplus or deficit of a club for the year.
explanation: False. It shows cash received and paid, including capital items, and no accruals or depreciation, so no surplus or deficit is found from it.

stem: The accumulated fund at the end of the year equals the opening accumulated fund plus the surplus of the year (when no other changes occur).
explanation: True. A surplus increases the fund; a deficit reduces it.

stem: Match each item in a club's records with the way it is treated.

left.content: Subscriptions in arrears at the start of the year
Expenses owing at the end of the year

right.content: Added to the cash paid to find the expense
Deducted when converting subscriptions received to income

explanation: Each adjustment moves a cash figure towards the figure that belongs to the year.

stem: Complete the statements about club accounts.

payload.template: A club's {{blank:a}} fund is its assets less its liabilities. An excess of income over expenditure is called a {{blank:b}}. The receipts and payments account shows {{blank:c}} items only.

explanation: Accumulated fund, surplus and cash items.

stem: At 1 July a club had equipment US\$5,200, furniture US\$2,700, bank US\$1,900, cash US\$70, subscriptions in arrears US\$180 and inventory US\$310. It owed US\$140 for expenses and had received US\$80 of subscriptions in advance. Calculate the accumulated fund.
hints: Total assets, then deduct the liabilities.

stem: A club had bank and cash of US\$2,300 at the start of the year. Receipts for the year totalled US\$14,200 and payments US\$13,350. Calculate the closing balance of bank and cash.
A club paid US\$5,100 for insurance in the year. It had a prepayment of US\$170 at the start of the year and has a prepayment of US\$230 at the end. Calculate the insurance expense for the year.
hints: The prepayment at the start is used up this year; the prepayment at the end is carried forward.

stem: A club's accumulated fund was US\$18,400 at the start of the year. It made a surplus of US\$2,900. Calculate the accumulated fund at the end of the year.
What is the club's equivalent of the owner's capital called?
explanation: A club has an accumulated fund instead of capital.

stem: State and explain two limitations of a receipts and payments account.

points.description: It shows cash only, so it does not show accruals or prepayments (1 mark)
It mixes capital and revenue items, so a surplus or deficit cannot be seen (1 mark)
It does not show the assets and liabilities, such as equipment or amounts owing (1 mark)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It shows cash only, ignoring accruals and prepayments. It mixes capital and revenue items so no surplus or deficit is shown. It also does not show assets and liabilities such as equipment or amounts owing.

explanation: One mark for each limitation explained.
hints: What is missing compared with an income and expenditure account?

stem: Explain why a club has an accumulated fund and not a capital account.

points.description: A club is not owned by individuals who invest in it for profit
Its net assets belong to the members collectively and arise from subscriptions and surpluses
The fund grows with surpluses and falls with deficits

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A club has no owners who invest to make a profit. Its net assets belong to the members collectively and arise from subscriptions and surpluses, so the fund grows with surpluses and falls with deficits.

explanation: One mark each for the absence of owners, the source of the fund and the effect of results.

stem: The treasurer says: "The club ended the year with US\$3,200 more in the bank, so it made a surplus of US\$3,200." Evaluate this statement.

points.description: The change in the bank balance is a cash movement and includes capital items such as equipment
Accruals, prepayments, arrears and depreciation are not in the cash movement
The income and expenditure account is needed to find the true surplus
Conclusion: the statement is not reliable; the surplus may be higher or lower than the increase in cash

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The increase in the bank balance includes capital payments and receipts and ignores accruals, prepayments, arrears and depreciation. The true surplus must be found from the income and expenditure account, so the statement is unreliable.

explanation: A balanced answer says why cash and surplus differ and concludes.

stem: Mutare Chess Club began the year with equipment US\$4,500, bank US\$2,100, cash US\$90 and subscriptions in arrears US\$170. It owed US\$140 for rent. During the year it received subscriptions of US\$3,600 and donations of US\$420, and paid rent US\$1,800, tournament costs US\$900 and US\$650 for new chess clocks. At the year end rent of US\$170 was owing.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the accumulated fund at the start of the year.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the closing balance of bank and cash.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the rent expense for the year.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why the cost of the new chess clocks is not charged as an expense in the income and expenditure account.

points.description: The clocks are equipment that will be used for several years (capital expenditure)
Only depreciation is charged each year
The clocks are shown as an asset in the statement of financial position

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The clocks will be used for several years, so they are capital expenditure. Only their depreciation is charged to the income and expenditure account and the clocks are an asset in the statement of financial position.

parts.explanation: One mark each for capital expenditure, depreciation and the asset.

explanation: This item practises the accumulated fund and conversion of cash items.
hints: The fund is assets less liabilities.
Use opening and closing accruals for the rent.

stem: Gweru Rugby Club's year ends on 30 June 2026. At 1 July 2025 it had pitch equipment US\$9,000, clubhouse fittings US\$4,000, bank US\$2,600, cash US\$100, subscriptions in arrears US\$300 and refreshment inventory US\$400. It owed the groundsman US\$250 and had received US\$100 of subscriptions in advance. Receipts for the year: subscriptions US\$9,800, proceeds of a fete US\$1,640, donations US\$650. Payments: groundsman US\$4,800, electricity US\$1,100, refreshments US\$1,500, new equipment US\$2,000, administration US\$700. At 30 June 2026: arrears US\$350, subscriptions in advance US\$160, groundsman owed US\$300, refreshment inventory US\$520. Depreciation is 10% on equipment at the year end (before depreciation) and 10% on the fittings.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the accumulated fund at 1 July 2025.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the closing balance of bank and cash at 30 June 2026.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Prepare the income and expenditure account for the year ended 30 June 2026.

points.description: Subscriptions 9,790 (own figure) and other income (fete 1,640, donations 650)
Groundsman's wages 4,850
Refreshments 1,380
Electricity and administration shown without adjustment
Depreciation 1,100 and 400
Total income 12,080, total expenditure 9,530 and surplus of 2,550

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Gweru Rugby Club: income and expenditure account for the year ended 30 June 2026**

|  | US\$ | US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Income |  |  |
| Subscriptions | 9,790 |  |
| Proceeds of the fete | 1,640 |  |
| Donations | 650 |  |
| Total income |  | 12,080 |
| Expenditure |  |  |
| Groundsman's wages | 4,850 |  |
| Electricity | 1,100 |  |
| Refreshments | 1,380 |  |
| Administration | 700 |  |
| Depreciation: equipment | 1,100 |  |
| Depreciation: fittings | 400 |  |
| Total expenditure |  | (9,530) |
| **Surplus for the year** |  | 2,550 |

parts.explanation: Each item is adjusted for opening and closing balances.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the accumulated fund at 30 June 2026.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Comment on the club's financial position using the surplus and the accumulated fund.

points.description: A surplus of 2,550 means income exceeded expenditure and the fund has grown by about 16%
The surplus relies partly on the fete (1,640) and donations (650), which may not repeat
The club should continue to monitor subscriptions and costs, and build the bank balance of 4,690

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The surplus of US\$2,550 increased the fund by about 16%, but part of the income came from the fete and donations, which may not be repeated. The club should keep subscriptions and costs under review.

parts.explanation: One mark each for the surplus, its reliability and a recommendation.

explanation: This item practises the accumulated fund and the conversion to an income and expenditure account.
hints: Convert each cash figure to the amount for the year.
Depreciation on equipment is calculated after adding the new purchases.
